descriptionChirho: A proper geographical name for Debir (Hebrew דְּבִיר), a Canaanite royal city in the southern hill country of Judah conquered by Joshua and later by Othniel (Josh 10:38-39, 11:21, 15:15-17; Judg 1:11-12). All three clusters are grammatical variants of the same toponym: the primary citation form 'Debir/Devir' (eng Devir/Debir, spa Debir/Devir, hin दबीर/दवीर-के, arb دَبيرَ/دَبِيرَ, kor 드빌의/드빌, swa Debiri), a dative/directional form 'to Debir' (eng to-Devir, spa a-Debir, hin दबीरा-को, arb لِ-دَبيرَ, kor 에게-드비르에게/드비르로, swa kwa-Debiri), and a suffixed variant 'Devirah' (eng Devirah, spa Debir, hin दबीरा, arb دَبيرةَ, kor 드빌로, swa Debiri). The Arabic and Hindi transliterations دَبيرَ/دَبِيرَ and दबीर/दवीर confirm these are all renderings of one place name.
